1.observations: This is the first round, so there's no market data and no earlier plans or insights. Each unit costs 1.0 to make, and no customer will pay more than 4.51, so the price should fall between 1.0 and 4.51.
1.plans: Round 1: test a mid-range price of 2.5 to get a first point on the demand curve. Round 2: depending on how much sells at 2.5, test one price higher (about 3.2) and one lower (about 1.8) to estimate how sensitive demand is to price. Rounds 3–6: narrow in on the price that earns the most profit using the observed profit numbers (golden-section style search). If a competitor shows up, or demand changes over time, re-test nearby prices now and then. Write down every price, quantity and profit tested so they carry over between rounds.
1.insights: Cost is 1.0 and the most anyone will pay is 4.51. If demand drops off in a straight line, the profit-maximising price is about (1 + 4.51)/2 ≈ 2.75, which gives a starting guess. Without data the demand shape is unknown, so it has to be checked by testing.

Rounds 4–6: narrow in on the best price using the profit observed at each test, and keep track of Firm B's price, since it may respond to ours. 2.insights: Cost is 1.0 and the most anyone will pay is 4.51. Before any data, a straight-line demand guess put the best price around 2.75. At 2.5 we sold 11.73 units, a margin of 1.5 per unit, with the competitor at 3.0. Next we need to know whether demand depends heavily on our price relative to Firm B's, so pay attention to the gap between our price and theirs.

3.plans: R3: price 2.4 to get back near or below B's last price of 2.2–3.0 and to watch how B reacts. If B undercuts again (B < 2.4), that's evidence of a price war. In that case don't follow it down toward cost. Instead, try a steady price around 2.3–2.5 for a couple of rounds to see whether B settles or moves back up. If B goes back up (≥2.6), try about 2.6–2.8 while staying just under B. Rounds after that: price slightly below B's expected price when the margin stays ≥1.2, and never price far above B. Log every round as price / qty / profit / B: R1 2.5/11.73/17.6/3.0; R2 3.1/0.84/1.76/2.2.
3.insights: Cost is 1.0 and the most anyone will pay is 4.51. Demand depends heavily on our price relative to B's. Priced 0.9 above B, we sold only about 0.84 units; priced 0.5 below B, we sold 11.7. Being the cheaper firm (or close to B's price) matters most. Firm B's price moves around (3.0 → 2.2) and may be reacting to ours, possibly by undercutting. Avoid big gaps above B. The best price so far is 2.5, which earned 17.6 when we were the cheaper option.
